claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared in a homogenized high-temperature BCC state by quenching from 1200°C.
The stability of the high-temperature BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a critical temperature window.
Within that critical temperature window, atomic mobility permits diffusion-driven elemental partitioning.
Diffusion-driven elemental partitioning triggers nucleation of secondary phases.
An intermediate exposure near 800°C creates local compositional fluctuations and precipitates in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Lower-temperature exposure preserves the original BCC structure by limiting diffusion.
Rapid quenching preserves the original BCC structure by suppressing significant elemental diffusion.
A rapid-quench rate of approximately 100°C/s freezes the high-temperature BCC state.
Slow cooling at approximately 1°C/s permits more atomic mobility than rapid quenching.
An intermediate isothermal hold near 1050°C enhances diffusion during slow cooling.
Local elemental partitioning and compositional fluctuations in the BCC matrix generate temperature-dependent nucleation sites.
Near 800°C, diffusion-controlled segregation reduces the free-energy barrier for secondary-phase nucleation.
A 600°C hold limits diffusion sufficiently to preserve metastable BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Specimens held at 800°C will contain measurable secondary phases relative to rapidly quenched specimens.
Slowly cooled specimens will contain measurable secondary phases relative to rapidly quenched specimens.
Samples held at 600°C will remain predominantly BCC, similarly to rapidly quenched samples.
Secondary-phase formation and associated compositional gradients can be detected using XRD, SEM/EDS, TEM, or APT.
The proposed explanation applies when diffusion dominates phase transformation and does not apply when oxidation or stress-induced effects become significant.
Oxidation can produce strongly time- and temperature-dependent secondary phases that are distinct from the proposed bulk partitioning mechanism.
The precise transformation threshold and kinetics may vary with minor composition changes, hold time, cooling rate, and internal stress.
